events.text:
**Go to Grand Haven.** The newest reports are 6 days old (2022-09-14), so these ratings are expectations, not observed conditions.

| Port | Expected rating | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| **Grand Haven** | **3 (good)** | Rated good in the latest report. |
| South Haven | 2 (average) | Decent but vague, with no fish depth reported. |
| Muskegon | 1 (below average) | Rated below average in the latest report. |
| St. Joseph | 1 (below average) | Only a couple of boats reported, with few fish. |

**Where and how at Grand Haven**
- Salmon action was decent 55–110 ft down in 120–210 ft of water (Grand Haven, 2022-09-14).
- Spoons in green, yellow and orange produced good numbers of salmon. Green and white flies worked well deeper in the water column (Grand Haven, 2022-09-14).
- The week before was average. Fish were 40–85 ft down in 40–120 ft of water on glow spoons and green or white flies (Grand Haven, 2022-09-07).
- Pier fishing was slow (Grand Haven, 2022-09-14), so stay on the boat.

**The other ports**
- **South Haven:** Boat anglers "had decent fishing when they could get out" (quality 2). The best water was around 110 ft, with a mixed bag of Chinook, coho and steelhead, mostly on spoons (South Haven, 2022-09-14). The report doesn't say how deep the fish were. The previous week was rated good, with fish in 110–120 ft and the best water around 40 ft, on spoons, rotators and flies (South Haven, 2022-09-07). If Grand Haven is too far, this is the second choice.
- **Muskegon:** Fish were 55–100 ft down in 100–200 ft of water on green and orange spoons and green flies. The report rated it below average (Muskegon, 2022-09-14). Fishing was average the week before (Muskegon, 2022-09-07). A few salmon were also caught jigging and trolling near the sand docks in Muskegon Lake (Muskegon, 2022-09-14).
- **St. Joseph:** A couple of boats fishing the pier heads caught a couple of coho and Chinook (St. Joseph, 2022-09-14). The previous week was also below average, with the best water around 100 ft on spoons (St. Joseph, 2022-09-07). The reports are thin, so the low rating may partly reflect few boats fishing.

**My read**
- I'd expect Grand Haven to stay the best of the four. It was the only port rated good this week, and it has been average to good for the last three reports.
- The buoys show surface water around 70–72 F at all four ports, nearly unchanged over the week (buoy summaries, 2022-09-20). That is well above the 52–58 F range Chinook and coho prefer (NY DEC, general guidance). I'd expect salmon to stay deep, in the 55–110 ft range the reports describe, rather than near the surface.
- Nothing in the buoy data points to an upwelling or a change in the bite.
- The South Haven rating is the least certain. "When they could get out" hints that weather limited trips, and the report gives no fish depth.

**Caveats**
- The tools returned no forecast, so I can't judge wind or waves. Check the marine forecast before you go.
- The tools returned no modeled cold-layer depth, so the fish depths above come from the reports only.
- The history search returned only this season's reports, so I have no earlier-season comparison for what usually happens next.
- I didn't call the Holland data, since you didn't ask about it.

- 2022-09-07: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/32bbcf0
